ai.summary: Nvidia says it has stopped shipping Hopper-series AI data-center chips to China, including the H200, despite earlier U.S. approval for sales. Its board has also formed a committee to oversee national-security policy and export-control compliance.
ai.title: Nvidia says it will stop selling some AI data center chips to China

ai.summary: OpenAI introduced GPT-6.2 Astra for complex work and GPT-6.2 Sol for everyday tasks, making both available through ChatGPT Work, Codex and its API. OpenAI says Astra’s API price is 20% lower than its predecessor and classifies it at the company’s “High” level for AI self-improvement risk.
ai.title: Introducing GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol

ai.summary: Nvidia reported fiscal third-quarter results and said it expects continued revenue growth, with its CEO describing demand as accelerating. The company also announced expanded supply-chain commitments to support AI infrastructure production.
ai.title: NVIDIA Announces Financial Results for Third Quarter Fiscal 2027

ai.summary: New U.S. Commerce Department rules require export licenses for certain advanced-chip and data-center services provided to China-linked customers. The rules also impose additional licensing requirements on facilities in several countries, aiming to limit access through overseas data centers.
ai.title: US tightens rules on chip exports. But divisions over AI and China persist.

ai.summary: Nvidia’s stronger-than-expected quarterly results and outlook did not settle investor concerns about the durability of the AI boom; its shares and other AI-linked stocks swung sharply. The market’s reaction highlights ongoing uncertainty around industry growth and valuations.
ai.title: Wall Street wobbles as Nvidia and other AI stocks keep swinging sharply

ai.summary: Nvidia announced new agreements with Kinsus and Samsung Electro-Mechanics to increase substrate capacity and expand production at existing factories. The move addresses supply-chain capacity as demand for AI infrastructure grows.
ai.title: NVIDIA Expands Commitments With Supply Chain Partners to Support AI Infrastructure Buildout

quantum.summary: Q-CTRL reports an experimental demonstration of magic-state cultivation with lattice-surgery escape on IBM’s Nighthawk processor. The company says the work set three records, including a cultivated-state error probability of 2 × 10⁻⁵; these are results reported by the researchers.
quantum.title: Cultivating record-fidelity magic states with lattice surgery on publicly accessible IBM quantum computers

quantum.summary: IBM, NVIDIA and Fermilab plan a codesign platform linking IBM quantum computers with NVIDIA accelerated systems to study error correction, modular architectures and scientific applications. NVIDIA also announced a decoder it says can speed some error-correction research workloads by up to 13,000 times.
quantum.title: NVIDIA, IBM and Fermilab advance modular quantum computing

quantum.summary: Researchers report teleporting a logical qubit between processors using lattice surgery on superconducting hardware, coordinating 41 physical qubits. Repeated stabilizer measurements were used to suppress errors during the transfer, a step toward modular fault-tolerant systems.
quantum.title: Logical Qubits Teleported With 41 Physical Qubits

quantum.summary: Alice & Bob announced a modular cat-qubit roadmap targeting 200 logical qubits by 2030, built from 3,600 physical qubits. The target is a company roadmap, not a delivered system; the firm says its architecture uses linked QPUs and cat qubits that suppress bit-flip errors.
quantum.title: Alice & Bob Unveils Accelerated Roadmap on Modular Architecture: 200 Logical Qubits from 3,600 Physical Qubits by 2030

quantum.source: Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory and QuEra (via All80sZ1063)
quantum.summary: QuEra and Berkeley Lab announced a Nature study using the Aquila neutral-atom processor with NERSC’s Perlmutter supercomputer to study quantum dynamics after a sudden change. The team reports observing a dynamical phase transition in a two-dimensional system.
quantum.title: QuEra Computing and Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory Publish Nature Study of Quantum Dynamics on Up to 180 Qubits

quantum.summary: Quandela, CNRS and NVIDIA researchers published a benchmark for when photonic quantum processors become harder to simulate exactly on a single NVIDIA H100 GPU. The study proposes a common throughput-based measure, aiming to make comparisons across photonic hardware and classical simulation methods more consistent.
quantum.title: Quandela and NVIDIA Benchmark Photonic Quantum Simulability Frontiers on H100 GPUs
